Bank-Math-Master.question: ১) A water tank has two taps (Tap-1 and Tap-2): Tap-1 can fill a tank in 6 hours and Tap- 2 can empty the tank in 12 hours. How long will they take to fill the tank if both taps are opened simultaneously but Tap-2 is closed after 6 hours?
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: A water tank has two taps (Tap-1 and Tap-2): Tap-1 can fill a tank in 6 hours and Tap- 2 can empty the tank in 12 hours. How long will they take to fill the tank if both taps are opened simultaneously but Tap-2 is closed after 6 hours?

Solution:
Tap-1, in 1 hour it fills = 1/6 part
Tap-2 in 1 hour it empties = 1/12 part

When both taps are open, in 1 hrs it fills = (1/6 - 1/12) part
= (2 -1)/12 part
= 1/12 part
When both taps are open, in 6 hrs it fills = {(1/12) × 6} part
= 1/2 part
∴ Remaining = (1 - 1/2) = 1/2 part

As Tap-2 is closed after 6 hours
∴ Tap-1, 1 part will be filled in = 6 hours
Remaining 1/2 part will be filled in = 6 × 1/2 = 3 hours

∴ Total time required = 6 + 3 = 9 hours

Bank-Math-Master.question: ২) A square and an equilateral triangle have equal perimeters. If the diagonal of the square is 12√2 cm, then the area of the triangle is-
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: A square and an equilateral triangle have equal perimeters. If the diagonal of the square is 12√2 cm, then the area of the triangle is-

Solution:
Let, the side of the square be a cm
Then, its diagonal √2a
√2a = 12√2
⇒ a = 12

∴ Perimeter of the square = 4a
= 4 × 12
= 48 cm

and also perimeter of the equilateral triangle = 48 cm

∴ Each side of the triangle = 48/3
= 16 cm

Area of the triangle = (√3/4) × (16)2 cm2
= (√3/4) × 256 cm2
= 64√3 cm2

Bank-Math-Master.question: ৩) A does 20% less work than B. If A can complete a piece of work in 15/2 hours, then B can do it in-
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: A does 20% less work than B. If A can complete a piece of work in 15/2 hours, then B can do it in-

Solution:
Ratio of times taken by A and B = 100/80 = 5/4
Let
B takes x days to do the work

ATQ,
5/4 = (15/2)/x
⇒ 5/4 = (15/2)/x
⇒ 5x = (15 × 4)/2
⇒ 5x = 30
∴ x = 6 hours

Bank-Math-Master.question: ৪) Two ingoing pipes can fill a tank in 4 and 6 hours, respectively. An outgoing pipe is attached to these two pipes and thus the tank was filled in 3 hours. In 60 hours the outgoing pipe alone can empty how many tanks?
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: Two ingoing pipes can fill a tank in 4 and 6 hours, respectively. An outgoing pipe is attached to these two pipes and thus the tank was filled in 3 hours. In 60 hours the outgoing pipe alone can empty how many tanks?

Solution:
Let,
the outgoing pipe take P hours to empty the tank.

So, in 1 hour total fillup = (1/4 + 1/6 - 1/P) part
= (5P - 12)/12P part

ATQ,
12P/(5P - 12) = 3
⇒ 12P = 15P - 36
⇒ 3P = 36
∴ P = 12

in 60 hours it can empty = 60/12 = 5 tanks

Bank-Math-Master.question: ৫) How many cubes of 10 cm edge can be put in a cubical box of 1 m edge?
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: How many cubes of 10 cm edge can be put in a cubical box of 1 m edge?

Solution:
Number of cubes = (100 × 100 × 100)/(10 × 10 × 10)
= 1000 cubes

[Note: 1 m = 100 cm]

Bank-Math-Master.question: ৬) A can do a piece of work in 24 days. When he had worked for 6 days, B joined him. If complete work was finished in 18 days, B can alone finish that work in-
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: A can do a piece of work in 24 days. When he had worked for 6 days, B joined him. If complete work was finished in 18 days, B can alone finish that work in-

Solution:
A's 1 day's work = 1/24 part
A's 18 day's work = 18/24 part
= 3/4 part

Remaining work = 1 - 3/4 = 1/4 part

1/4 part work done by B in = (18 - 6) = 12 days
∴ 1 part work done by B in = (12 × 4) = 48 days

Bank-Math-Master.question: ৭) The length of a ractangle is 20% more than its breadth. What will be the ratio of the area of a rectangle to that of a square whose side is equal to the breadth of the rectangle?
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: The length of a ractangle is 20% more than its breadth. What will be the ratio of the area of a rectangle to that of a square whose side is equal to the breadth of the rectangle?

Solution:
Let,
breadth be x metres
∴ length = (120% of x) metres
= 120x/100 metres
= 6x/5 metres

∴ the area of the rectangle = (6x/5 × x) m2

∴ the area of the square = (x × x) m2

∴ The ratio = (6x/5 × x) : (x × x)
= 6 : 5

Bank-Math-Master.question: ৮) Two pipes can fill a tank with water in 15 and 12 hours respectively and a third pipe can empty it in 4 hours. If the three pipes be opened, the tank will be emptied in-
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: Two pipes can fill a tank with water in 15 and 12 hours respectively and a third pipe can empty it in 4 hours. If the three pipes be opened, the tank will be emptied in-

Solution:
Part of the tank filled by two pipes in 1 hour = 1/15 + 1/12
= (4 + 5)/60 part
= 9/60 part
= 3/20
Part of the tank emptied by the third pipe in 1 hour = 1/4

∴ Net part of the tank emptied in 1 hour = (1/4 - 3/20) part
= (5 - 3)/20 part
= 2/20 part
= 1/10 part

1/10 Part of tank can be emptied in 1 hour
∴ The whole tank will be filled in = 10 hours

Bank-Math-Master.question: ৯) A and B can do a piece of work in 28 days and 35 days respectively. They began to work together but A leaves after some time and B completed the remaining work in 17 days. After how many days did A leave?
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: A and B can do a piece of work in 28 days and 35 days respectively. They began to work together but A leaves after some time and B completed the remaining work in 17 days. After how many days did A leave?

Solution:
Work done by B in 17 days = {(1/35) × 17} part
= 17/35 part

Remaining work = (1 - 17/35) part
= 18/35 part

(A + B)'s 1 day's work = (1/28 + 1/35) part
= 9/140 part

Now,
9/140 part work has done by (A + B) in 1 day
∴ 1 part work has done by (A + B) in 140/9 days
∴ 18/35 part work has done by (A + B) in = {(140/9) × (18/35)} days
= 8 days

∴ A leave After 8 days

Bank-Math-Master.question: ১০) If the area of the trapezium, whose parallel sides are 6 cm and 10 cm is 64 sq. cm, what will be the distance between the parallel sides?
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: If the area of the trapezium, whose parallel sides are 6 cm and 10 cm is 64 sq. cm, what will be the distance between the parallel sides?

Solution:
Given,
Parallel sides of a trapezium = 6 cm, and 10 cm

We know,
Area of trapezium = (1/2)(sum of the parallel sides) × distance between the parallel sides
64 = (1/2)(6 + 10) × distance
⇒ 64 = 8 × distance
⇒ distance = 64/8
∴ distance = 8 cm

So, the distance between the parallel lines of trapezium = 8 cm.

Bank-Math-Master.question: ১১) One pipe can fill a tank four times as fast as another pipe. If together the two pipes can fill the tank in 36 minutes, then the faster pipe alone will be able to fill the tank in:
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: One pipe can fill a tank four times as fast as another pipe. If together the two pipes can fill the tank in 36 minutes, then the faster pipe alone will be able to fill the tank in:

Solution:
Let,
the slower pipe alone fill the tank in x minutes.
Then, Faster pipe alone will fill it in x/4 minutes.

ATQ,
(1/x) + (4/x) = 1/36
⇒ 5/x = 1/36 
∴ x = 180

The slower pipe alone fill the tank in 180 minutes.
the faster pipe alon will be able to fill the tank in = (180 ÷ 4) minutes.
= 45 minutes

Bank-Math-Master.question: ১২) If the volume of a sphere is divided by its surface area, the result is 27 cm. the radius of the sphere is-
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: If the volume of a sphere is divided by its surface area, the result is 27 cm. the radius of the sphere is-

Solution:
Let,
the radius of the sphere is r cm
∴ the volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr3
∴ the surface area of a sphere = 4πr2

ATQ,
{(4/3)πr3}/(4πr2) = 27
⇒ r/3 = 27
∴ r = 81

∴ the radius of the sphere is 81 cm

Bank-Math-Master.question: ১৩) A can complete a piece of work in 18 days, B in 20 days and C in 30 days. B and C together start the work and are forced to leave after 2 days. The time taken by A alone to complete the remaining work is-
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: A can complete a piece of work in 18 days, B in 20 days and C in 30 days. B and C together start the work and are forced to leave after 2 days. The time taken by A alone to complete the remaining work is-

Solution:
Here,
B's 1 day's work = 1/20 part
C's 1 day's work = 1/30 part

∴ (B + C)'s 1 day's work = (1/20 + 1/30) part
∴ (B+C)'s 2 day's work = {(1/20 + 1/30) × 2} part
= [{(3+2)/60} × 2] part
= (5/60 × 2) part
= 1/6 part

Remaining work = (1 -1/6) part
= 5/6 part

A's one day's work = 1/18 part
∴ The time taken by A alone to complete the remaining work is = (5/6)/(1/18) days
= 15 days

Bank-Math-Master.question: ১৪) 55 men can finish a work in 42 days. How many additional men must be engaged to complete the work 9 days earlier?
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: 55 men can finish a work in 42 days. How many additional men must be engaged to complete the work 9 days earlier?

Solution:
Here,
Days needed = (42 - 9) = 33 days

To complete the work in 42 days, it requires 55 men
To complete the work in 1 days, it requires (55 × 42) men
To complete the work in 33 days, it requires (55× 42)/33 men
= 70 men

∴ additional men required = (70 - 55) men
= 15 men

Bank-Math-Master.question: ১৫) 15 buckets of water fill a tank when the capacity of each bucket is 15 litres. How many buckets will be needed to fill the same tank, if the capacity of each bucket is 25 liters?
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: 15 buckets of water fill a tank when the capacity of each bucket is 15 litres. How many buckets will be needed to fill the same tank, if the capacity of each bucket is 25 liters?

Solution:
The capacity of the tank = (15 x 15) litres
= 225 litres

The capacity of each bucket = 25 litres
Number of buckets needed = (225 ÷ 25) = 9

Bank-Math-Master.question: ১৬) How many bricks need to build a wall 8 m long, 6 m high and 11 cm thick, where as each bricks measuring 25 cm × 60 cm × 11 cm?
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: How many bricks need to build a wall 8 m long, 6 m high and 11 cm thick, where as each bricks measuring 25 cm × 60 cm × 11 cm?

Solution:
Given,
Wall long = 8 m = 800 cm
Wall thick = 11 cm
Wall high = 6 m = 600 cm

∴ Volume of the wall = (800 × 600 × 11) cm3

∴ Volume of the brick = 25 cm × 11 cm × 60 cm

∴ bricks need to build the wall = Volume of the wall ÷ Volume of the brick
= (800 × 600 × 11) ÷ (25 × 11 × 60)
= 320

Bank-Math-Master.question: ১৭) If A can do 1/4 of a work in 3 days and B can do 1/9 of the same work in 4 days, how much will A get if both work together and paid Tk 800 in all?
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: If A can do 1/4 of a work in 3 days and B can do 1/9 of the same work in 4 days, how much will A get if both work together and paid Tk 800 in all?

Solution:
Whole work is done by A in (3 × 4) = 12 days
∴ A's 1 day's work = 1/12 part
Whole work is done by B in (4 × 9) = 36 days
∴ B's 1 day's work = 1/36 part

A's 1 day's work : B's 1 day's work
= A's wages : B's wages
= 1/12 : 1/36
= 3 : 1

∴ A's share = (800 × 3/4) Tk
= 600 Tk

Bank-Math-Master.question: ১৮) A pipe can fill a cistern in 16 hours. After half the tank is filled, three more similar taps are opened. What is the total time taken to fill the cistern completely?
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: A pipe can fill a cistern in 16 hours. After half the tank is filled, three more similar taps are opened. What is the total time taken to fill the cistern completely?

Solution:
Time is taken to fill half of the tank = (1/2) × 16 = 8 hrs

In 1 hour 1 pipe can fill = 1/16 part
∴ In 1 hour 4 pipe can fill = {4 × (1/16)} part
= 1/4 part

4 pipe can fill 1/4 part in 1 hour
∴ 4 pipe can fill 1 part in 4 hour
∴ 4 pipe can fill 1/2 part in (4 × 1/2) hour
= 2 hours

∴ Total time = (8 + 2) = 10 hours.

Bank-Math-Master.question: ১৯) A garrison of 600 men had provisions for 30 days. After 3 days a reinforcement of 300 men arrived. How many days will the remaining food last now?
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: A garrison of 600 men had provisions for 30 days. After 3 days a reinforcement of 300 men arrived. How many days will the remaining food last now?

Solution:
After 3 days, food having for = (30 - 3) = 27 days
After arriving 300 men, total men = (600 + 300) = 900 men

600 men can eat the food for 27 days
∴ 1 man can eat the food for (27 × 600) days
∴ 900 men can eat the food for (27 × 600)/900 days
= 18 days

Bank-Math-Master.question: ২০) Five equal cubes, each of side 5 cm, are placed adjacent to each other. The volume of the new solid formed will be-
Bank-Math-Master.exp:
Question: Five equal cubes, each of side 5 cm, are placed adjacent to each other. The volume of the new solid formed will be-

Solution:
The new formed is a cuboid of length = 5 × 5 = 25 cm
breadth = 5 cm and height = 5 cm

∴ Volume = (25 × 5 × 5) cm3
= 625 cm3
